name: Davco Powder Mastic
paste:
DAVCO® POWDER MASTIC: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Davco® Powder Mastic, May 2025, Version 01.01 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/h/davco-powder-mastic.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Davco® Powder Mastic where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (May 2025, Version 01.01).
1.2 Product description. A flexible, cement-based tile adhesive ideal for large format and rectified edge tiles equipped with DUST LESS technology which reduces airborne dust by up to 80% in the mixing phase.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. Davco® Powder Mastic is suitable for interior and exterior applications. Commercial and domestic walls and floors including high foot traffic locations, bathrooms, showers, kitchens, laundries, living rooms, balconies and patios. Davco® Powder Mastic is suitable for most common substrates including;
    - fibre cement sheet / Ceramic Tile Underlay
    - Fully cured concrete
    - Screed (cured for 7 days)
    - Rendered brickwork and blockwork
    - Suitable Sika under tile waterproofing membranes and acoustic underlays.
    - Large format and rectified (square) edge tiles
    - Porcelain
    - Ceramic
    - Mosaic
    - Natural stone (not sensitive to moisture)
    Davco® Powder Mastic is ideal for most types of tiles including

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Davco® Powder Mastic
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals, certificates and standards stated by the manufacturer. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (May 2025, Version 01.01) has no approvals, certificates or standards section.
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - AS ISO 13007.1: cited with a stated property or value. Where: Product Information > Product Declaration (p.1).
    - SCAQMD method 304-91: cited with a stated property or value. Where: Product Information > Volatile organic compound (VOC) content (p.1).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - DUST LESS technology, less mess and airborne dust when mixing
    - Commercial grade
    - Dust Less Technology
    - Non-vertical slump for easy wall tiling
    - Use for thick or thin bed tiling
    - Extended open time for tiling large areas
    - White formulation ideal for light coloured tiles and stone
2.5 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Appearance / Colour: White powder
    - Product Declaration: C1TES1 - AS ISO 13007.1
    - Volatile organic compound (VOC) content: Low VOC - 7g/L (SCAQMD method 304-91)
2.6 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 20kg bags
    - Shelf life: 12 Months from date of manufacture if unopened
    - Storage conditions: Store in off ground in dry cool conditions out of direct sunlight

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (May 2025, Version 01.01) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate preparation.
    - All surfaces must be installed according to manufacturer’s instructions and relevant Australian Standard(s) and be structurally sound, dry, clean and free from movement, oil, grease, wax, curing compounds, release agents and any other loose or contaminating material. Thoroughly clean old surfaces, or new surfaces that have been treated, prior to tiling
    - Deeply contaminated surfaces must be scabbled / abraded to a clean, sound surface. Expose at least 80% of the original substrate of painted surfaces
    - Surfaces should be prepared and primed as per the following:
    | Substrate | Specific requirement | Priming |
    | Concrete - wood float finish | Cured minimum 6 weeks | Prime with Davco PrimeX or Ul- |
    | (rough) | traprime |
    | Concrete – steel trowel finish | Cured minimum 6 weeks Free of | Prime with Davco PrimeX |
    | (smooth) | laitance (not flaking) |
    | Rendered brick / blockwork - wood float finish | Cured minimum 24 hours Sound (Not drummy or | Prime with Davco PrimeX or Ultraprime |
    | (rough) | cracked) |
    | Screed - wood float finish | Cured minimum 7 days Sound | Prime with Davco PrimeX or Ul- |
    | (rough) | (Not drummy or cracked) | traprime |
    | Fibre cement sheet, plasterboard | Correctly and firmly fixed | Prime with Davco PrimeX or Ultraprime |
    | Compressed fibre cement sheet | Correctly and firmly fixed | Prime with Davco PrimeX |
    | Timber floor | Lined with Ceramic Tile Underlay or suitable screed system (no direct fixing to timber flooring) | Prime with Davco PrimeX |
    | Other difficult / non absorbent | Where not feasible to remove | Prime with Davco Ultrabond or |
    | (e.g. metal) / contaminated (e.g. old flooring or tile adhesive) | Sika Prep n Prime |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
    Refer to the primer product datasheet for additional information.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (May 2025, Version 01.01) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Mixing Ratio: 5-6 Litres of clean cool potable water per 20kg
    - Consumption: 20kg bag of Davco® Powder Mastic covers approximately 7 m² (based on a 10mm notch trowel)
    - Pot Life: 2 Hours
    - Open Time: 30 Minutes
4.3 Applied Product Ready for Use.
    | Application | Wait time |
    | Light foot traffic | 24 hours |
    | Prior to grouting | 24 hours |
    | Return to dry are service | 24 hours |
    | Return to wet area service | 7 days |
    All measurements are taken at 22ºC and 50% relative humidity. Specifications vary according to site conditions and should be taken as a guide only.
4.4 Equipment.
    - Personal protective equipment
    - Mixing drill with stirrer attachment
    - Notched trowel
    - Mixing buckets
4.5 Mixing. 1. Measure the required amount of clean, potable water into a clean bucket. 2. Slowly add the powder into the water while mixing with a mixing paddle attached to a drill. Always add the powder to the liquid. Do not mix by hand. 3. Continue to mix for several minutes until a creamy consistency is achieved, free of lumps of powder. 4. Allow mixture to stand for 5 minutes, remix then use the adhesive.
    - Do not add any additional water during the adhesive's pot life, restir without adding water.
4.6 Application. Laying the tiles 1. Deposit a quantity of adhesive onto the prepared substrate. Do not apply more adhesive than can be tiled within the open time of the product, usually from a single tile up to around 1m² at a time. 2. Hold the notched trowel at an angle of 60° or greater to the substrate. 3. Spread the adhesive over the area where tile is to be applied, forming straight rows of adhesive “beads”. 4. Where “back buttering” is required, use the straight side of the trowel to apply a thin covering of adhesive to the back of the tile. 5. Position the tile on the beaded adhesive and press firmly. 6. Move the tile forward and then back at 90° across the direction of the beads to ensure all beads are flattened leaving no voids under the tile. Occasionally lift a tile after placing it to check that the beads are fully compressed and that sufficient coverage has been achieved (90–100%). Replace the tile. 7. After laying a section at a time, remove any excess adhesive from the grout joint and the surface of the tiles with a damp cloth while the adhesive is still wet.
    - Allow product to gain initial set before grouting
    - Allow product to set firmly before return to service
4.7 Cleaning of tools. Clean tools and equipment with water before the adhesive dries.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, confirm the site conditions with the manufacturer. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Conditions to be verified. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (May 2025, Version 01.01) lists no application condition limits.
5.3 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.4 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Davco® Powder Mastic, May 2025, Version 01.01, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/h/davco-powder-mastic.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Various Semi-Finished, version 19/11/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/q/sds-various-semi-finished-1.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Davco Powder Mastic, version 19/11/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/7/sds-davco-powdermastic.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.1, and include the records in the project documentation.
